v.t: Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth him; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: I would that ye all spake with tongues, but rather that ye prophesied: for greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Now, brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, except I shall speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophesying, or by doctrine?

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: And even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: So likewise ye, except ye utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye shall speak into the air.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without signification.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Therefore if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh shall be a barbarian unto me.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Even so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual gifts, seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Wherefore let him that speaketh in an unknown tongue pray that he may interpret.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Else when thou shalt bless with the spirit, how shall he that occupieth the room of the unlearned say Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he understandeth not what thou sayest?

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For thou verily givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all:

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Brethren, be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).
tm.ot: Closely echoes Isa 28:11 (42 reader votes, OpenBible.info).

v.t: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: If therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those that are unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that ye are mad?

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all:

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: How is it then, brethren? when ye come together, every one of you hath a psalm, hath a doctrine, hath a tongue, hath a revelation, hath an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Let the prophets speak two or three, and let the other judge.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: If any thing be revealed to another that sitteth by, let the first hold his peace.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For ye may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be comforted.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: And if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: What? came the word of God out from you? or came it unto you only?

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: If any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Wherefore, brethren, covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).

v.t: Let all things be done decently and in order.

tm.apostle: Letter written by Paul, called to be an apostle (1 Cor 1:1).
